P1.text: Step 1 (dev), the core: when the caller passes no `scripts`, the generated virtual:brumate/routes module supplies a default. An explicit `scripts` string (including '') still wins, so custom servers and CSP nonce setups keep control. Fixes the plain-vite-dev and own-server dev cases in 6 examples, 3 docs pages, 2 benchmarks, website/scripts/dev.ts.

P6.text: Step 3 (replaces rejected P3; A2 folded in): configureServer returns a post-middleware that answers GET/HEAD page requests in vite dev by importing virtual:brumate/routes through the SSR environment, calling handle(Request) (default scripts from P1), and piping the web ReadableStream to the Node response, so streaming is kept (idlip buffers; brumate does not). It falls through with next() when handle returns undefined, so Vite's own files, /@vite/client and the RPC POSTs of vite.ts:2759 are untouched. (a) Own server: skip when `server.config.server.middlewareMode` is true, which is exactly the setup of every example server.ts (createServer({server:{middlewareMode:true}, appType:'custom'})); an app that wants its own handler therefore never gets a second answer, and an option `pages: false` turns the middleware off in normal mode. A post-middleware also runs only after the app's own pre-middleware had a chance to end the response. (b) Nitro: skip when `server.environments.nitro` exists, which Nitro's dev plugin reads at _build/vite.dev.mjs:76 and creates itself; Nitro's worker then renders with the P1 default, since the routes module is generated in the Vite process (O4 ruled). Both checks are plain config reads at configureServer time, no request-time guess.

O8.text: Vite's default appType is 'spa' (the plugin never sets appType), and in that mode htmlFallbackMiddleware rewrites req.url to /index.html for every GET/HEAD whose Accept is empty, text/html or */*, before postHooks run (node.js:25115-25116: fallback first, then postHooks). A post-middleware that builds its Request from req.url would match no route for any page. P6 must build the URL from req.originalUrl, or the plugin must set appType 'custom' in its config hook; the 6 examples avoid this today only because they pass appType 'custom'. Both options need a test in plain `vite dev` with the default appType.

evidence.detail: spaFallback sets req.url = '/index.html' unconditionally; post hooks run after it

O9.text: P6 limits the middleware to GET and HEAD, but handleRoute serves every method: middleware, endpoints, a form's server function and the page share one event, and the hand-written servers pass every request that Vite did not consume to handle. A GET/HEAD-only plugin middleware would 404 POST/PUT route endpoints and no-JS form posts in plain `vite dev`, a regression once P8 deletes server.ts. Answer all methods the route tree matches and only call next() when handle returns undefined; this also changes the 'three modes e2e' scope of P6 to include a POST endpoint and a form post.

evidence.detail: hand server calls handle for any method; handleRoute matches endpoints and forms for all methods

P11.text: Amends P6 with O8, O9, O11. The plugin sets `appType: 'custom'` in its config hook when the user left appType unset (as SvelteKit does, J11), so Vite's SPA html fallback never rewrites req.url to /index.html before the post-middleware and the routes see the real URL; the plugin never overrides an appType the user set. A user who set 'spa' or 'mpa' gets no pages middleware and a one-time dev warning that brumate pages need appType 'custom' (the same middlewareMode skip as P6(a), so no double answer). The middleware answers every method and every Accept: it calls handle(Request) and falls through with next() only when handle returns undefined, so POST server function calls, endpoints, fetch() requests and non-HTML routes reach the routes module and Vite's own files, /@vite/client and RPC still fall through. P6's other parts (Nitro skip via server.environments.nitro, errorPage, streaming pipe) stay.

estimate.unit: day added to P6, size S; P10 total read as 6-10 days, e2e repointing of the examples is the main cost
